title: Purview policy and label resolution
purpose: Decision path from an access request through tenant/domain policy, workspace and item authorization, supported data-level controls, label resolution, and protected export.
accessibleSummary: Purview policy and label resolution. Access request; Delegated domain setting; Workspace and item scope; Data security supported?; Resolve sensitivity label; Enforce effective state; Export and unlabeled risk.
longDescription: Decision path from an access request through tenant/domain policy, workspace and item authorization, supported data-level controls, label resolution, and protected export.

nodes.label: Access request
nodes.summary: A user or workload attempts to open an item or query its data.
nodes.detail: Identity, workspace role, item permission, and the requested operation establish the authorization context.
nodes.whyItMatters: Governance begins with effective access, not with a label alone.

evidence.note: Fabric combines workspace access with row-, column-, and table-level controls on supported data items.

processing: Pass the authorized request to data-level controls
drill.example: A regional analyst opens a certified sales semantic model from its workspace.
failureModes: A broad workspace role grants more item access than intended.

nodes.label: Delegated domain setting
nodes.summary: A domain can override only governance settings delegated from the tenant level.
nodes.detail: Tenant administrators establish defaults; domain administrators apply permitted overrides for their business area.
nodes.whyItMatters: The branch separates centrally fixed policy from legitimately delegated policy.

evidence.note: Domains may apply governance settings delegated from the tenant.

processing: Check whether the setting is delegated
drill.example: Finance applies its delegated certification workflow while retaining tenant-wide DLP.
failureModes: Assuming every tenant setting can be overridden.

nodes.label: Workspace and item scope
nodes.summary: Workspace roles and item permissions narrow who can reach the governed item.
nodes.detail: The request is evaluated at workspace and item boundaries before supported data rules.
nodes.whyItMatters: This is where ownership and sharing mistakes surface.

evidence.note: Fabric governance spans domains, workspaces and item-level metadata and access surfaces.

drill.example: A viewer discovers a warehouse but can query only when the item owner grants access.
failureModes: Confusing catalog visibility with query permission.

nodes.label: Data security supported?
nodes.summary: RLS, CLS and TLS are available only on supported Fabric item types.
nodes.detail: The item type determines whether granular policies can further restrict an authorized query.
nodes.whyItMatters: The decision prevents promising controls the serving item does not implement.

evidence.note: RLS, CLS and TLS are supported for SQL analytics endpoints, warehouses, Direct Lake, and KQL Database items.

drill.example: A warehouse query proceeds to RLS evaluation.
failureModes: Designing around an unavailable security feature.

nodes.label: Resolve sensitivity label
nodes.summary: Labels may be manual, defaulted, inherited, or applied programmatically.
nodes.detail: Purview Information Protection supplies classification independently of access.
nodes.whyItMatters: A consistent label path keeps protection attached to data.

evidence.note: Sensitivity labels can be manual, defaulted, inherited, or programmatic.

drill.example: A lakehouse inherits Confidential from its governed upstream source.
failureModes: Unlabeled items provide no downstream classification signal.

nodes.label: Enforce effective state
nodes.summary: Authorization, data security, and label policy converge on the allowed operation.
nodes.detail: Supported filters restrict returned data while the label informs protection and governance handling.

processing: Apply supported filters and protection policy
drill.example: The analyst receives only its region's rows from a Confidential table.
failureModes: Treating a label as an access grant.

nodes.label: Export and unlabeled risk
nodes.summary: Supported exports retain label protection; an unlabeled path loses that safeguard.
nodes.detail: This warning contrasts protected export with inconsistent label coverage.
nodes.whyItMatters: Exports can leave the managed analytics boundary.

evidence.note: Label protection follows supported exports and can enforce encryption for authorized users.

processing: Verify label and supported export path
drill.example: A Confidential report exported to PDF remains restricted.
failureModes: An unlabeled item is exported without intended protection.

edges.label: Supported: apply RLS, CLS or TLS
